# Filing

`admin.obj.statutory_filing.filing` · v1.0.0 · **draft** · scope **capability**

> One submission of one prescribed form to one authority in one jurisdiction for one defined period. The discriminators are all external: the authority sets the form, the period and the date, and the penalty accrues by operation of law rather than by anyone deciding to apply it. Two properties follow from that and shape every rule below. First, a filing is not complete when it is sent; it is complete when the authority acknowledges it, and the gap between those two states is where late filings hide in plain sight. Second, the obligation does not depend on there being anything to report — a nil return is a filing, and dormant entities generate more penalties per head than trading ones for exactly that reason.


Also called: `Statutory Return`, `Regulatory Submission`, `Return`, `Declaration`

## Constraints

- **`fil.date_is_not_negotiable`** The statutory date cannot be moved by prioritisation,escalation or agreement with anyone inside the organisation.
- **`fil.signatory_role_required`** Only the role named by the regime may authorise thesubmission.
- **`fil.no_submission_without_approval`** A return may not be submitted before the recordedapproval exists. Filing first and papering it after is the single most common audit finding in this capability.
- **`fil.closure_requires_acknowledgement`** The obligation may not be marked dischargedwithout an acknowledgement reference.
- **`fil.filed_copy_is_retained`** The exact document submitted must be retained for thestatutory retention period, not a regenerated equivalent.
- **`fil.agent_delegation_is_operational_only`** Delegating submission to an agent doesnot delegate the obligation or the liability.


## Business rules

- **`fil.acknowledgement_is_the_filing`** A submission without a recorded acknowledgement reference is not a filing. Until the reference exists the organisation's position is that nothing was filed, and it should be reported that way internally however uncomfortable that is at month end.

- **`fil.nil_return_still_due`** A nil return is a filing. Having nothing to report suspends nothing. This rule exists because dormant entities generate more penalties per head than trading ones, entirely through this misunderstanding.

- **`fil.rejection_does_not_reset_the_clock`** A rejected submission leaves the original statutory date in force. The remaining window is the original window minus the time spent waiting to be told, which is why the internal target must absorb one full rejection cycle.

- **`fil.signatory_role_is_not_delegable`** Where the regime names a signing role, approval from any other role is not approval. The submission will be accepted by the portal and rejected by the authority, usually after the date.

- **`fil.internal_target_precedes_statutory_date`** internal_target_at must precede statutory_due_at by at least one full rejection-and-resubmission cycle for the channel in use.
- **`fil.agent_does_not_transfer_liability`** Delegating submission to an agent transfers the work and none of the obligation. An agent who has gone quiet is our problem on the statutory date and nobody else's.

- **`fil.penalty_accrues_without_notice`** Daily-accrual penalties do not wait for a reminder from the authority, and the first notice frequently arrives months later with the full accrual attached. Absence of correspondence is not evidence of compliance.

- **`fil.event_driven_obligations_need_a_trigger`** Event-driven filings — director changes, registered office moves, share allotments — have no recurring date to diarise and must be triggered by the event itself. This is the category where a competent filing calendar still fails.

## Actions

- **Assemble the return** (human) — Pull the period data and reconcileit to the source system before anyone is asked to sign.
- **Chase the blocking dependency** (agent) — The audit,the board resolution, the payroll close. Chasing the return before its dependency is theatre.
- **Request approval from the named signatory** (agent) — Names the role the statute requires, not the most available senior person.
- **Submit to the authority** (human) — Through the declared channel.The channel decides what counts as the filing date.
- **Record the acknowledgement reference** (system) — The step that actually closes the obligation and the one most often skipped, because by then everyone has moved on.
- **Request an extension** (human) — Where the regime allowsone, and before the date — an extension requested late is itself a late filing.
- **File a nil return** (human) — For a period with nothingto report. Cheapest filing in the calendar and the most frequently missed.
- **Escalate to the accountable officer** (human) — Mandatorywhere penalty_is_personal — the person carrying the liability is entitled to know before the date, not after.

## Metrics

- **on_time_filing_rate** (percent) — Share acknowledged on or before the statutorydate. Measured on acceptance, never on submission.
- **median_buffer_days** (days) — Days between acknowledgement and the statutorydate. A programme running at one day of buffer is not compliant, it is lucky.
- **rejection_rate** (percent) — Share of submissions rejected first time. Directlysets the buffer every filing needs.
- **acknowledgement_capture_rate** (percent) — Share of submissions with a referencerecorded. Measures the evidence discipline that the audit will actually test.
- **penalty_incurred** (money) —
- **preparation_cycle_days** (days) — Dependency ready to submission. Distinguishesa slow team from a blocked one.
- **nil_return_miss_rate** (percent) — Nil returns missed as a share of nil returnsdue. The cheapest number on this list to drive to zero.


## Examples

- **UK Confirmation Statement CS01** — Annual, fixed date, escalating consequence endingin strike-off and director disqualification. Ten minutes of work carrying an existential penalty.
- **Quarterly VAT return** — Recurring, percentage-of-liability penalty, dependency on aledger close. The routine one that trains a team to assume all filings behave like this one.
- **Monthly PF and ESI returns** — Short window, daily accrual, payroll dependency. Beingthree days late every month costs more than being three weeks late once a year, and looks less serious.
- **Annual accounts contingent on audit sign-off** — The classic dependency failure. Thefiling is reported green while the audit it waits on is amber.
- **Nil return for a dormant subsidiary** — nil_return_required = true, owner unassigned.The single highest-frequency penalty in any group holding dormant entities.
- **Change of registered office** — recurrence = event_driven. A short clock starting froman event nobody diarised, because the event had not happened when the calendar was built.

> Three of ten patterns are executable and all three run on commitment.due_at — a date a human typed into a task. That is the honest state of statutory filing on this substrate. The ranked asks are obligation.due_at (no statutory date feed exists anywhere in the stack), filing_accepted (portals already email a parseable acknowledgement and nothing reads it, so `submitted` and `filed` are indistinguishable), and filing_rejected (the highest-urgency event this object can generate, currently arriving as an email in one person's inbox). Modelling note: `files_with` targets admin.obj.core.stakeholder because the roster has no regulator or authority object; the authority is not a stakeholder in any ordinary sense — it is a counterparty with statutory power — and a future roster should carry admin.obj.core.authority instead.
